blogs.title: From 16‑bit to 1‑bit: How BitNet b1.58 Shrinks LLMs Without Losing Accuracy
blogs.description: An easy‑to‑read explainer on the core idea behind BitNet b1.58 – turning every weight into a ternary value (‑1, 0, +1). We'll walk through why this reduces memory and compute, how the 1.58‑bit representation works, and why the model still matches full‑precision perplexity and downstream task performance.

blogs.title: Energy‑Efficient AI: The Massive Power Savings of 1‑bit Large Language Models
blogs.description: A deep dive into the energy model behind BitNet b1.58. We'll compare the arithmetic energy costs of FP16 matrix multiplications versus INT8 additions, show the 70× reduction in multiplication energy, and discuss what this means for data‑center sustainability and carbon footprints.

blogs.title: Scaling Law Reimagined: Why a 13B BitNet b1.58 Beats a 3B FP16 LLM
blogs.description: Explore the new scaling law introduced by the authors. The post will break down the empirical equivalence table (e.g., 13B 1.58‑bit ≈ 3B FP16), explain why latency, memory, and energy improve superlinearly with size, and what this implies for future LLM development strategies.

blogs.title: Deploying LLMs on the Edge: How 1.58‑bit Models Make Mobile AI Feasible
blogs.description: Translate the technical advantages of BitNet b1.58 into a consumer‑focused story about running powerful language models on smartphones and IoT devices. Topics include reduced SRAM/DRAM bandwidth, 8‑bit activations, CPU friendliness, and potential real‑world applications.

blogs.title: Designing Hardware for 1‑bit LLMs: From GPUs to Dedicated LPUs
blogs.description: A forward‑looking piece on the hardware implications of a multiplication‑free transformer. We'll outline how current GPUs use 2‑bit kernels, what a custom ‘BitLinear’ accelerator could look like, and why companies like Groq are poised to benefit from a new generation of AI chips.

blogs.title: Quantization Tricks Explained: The AbsMean Function Behind Ternary Weights
blogs.description: Demystify the quantization pipeline that forces weights into {‑1, 0, +1}. The article will illustrate the absmean scaling, rounding/clipping steps with simple code snippets, and discuss why adding a zero value (the “0” in 1.58‑bit) improves feature filtering and model capacity.
